title: Count Coin Combinations
statement: You run a vending machine stocked with an unlimited supply of coins in each of several distinct denominations. Given a list of distinct positive integer denominations `coins` and a non-negative integer `amount`, return the number of distinct multisets of coins that sum to exactly `amount`. Two ways are considered the same if they use the same count of each denomination; the order in which coins are chosen does not matter (so paying 3 with a 1 then a 2 is the same as a 2 then a 1). Each denomination may be used any number of times, including zero. Return 1 when `amount` is 0 (the empty selection), and return 0 when no selection sums to `amount`.
hints: Counting selections where order does not matter is a counting DP over amounts. What subproblem would let dp[a] be the number of ways to make amount a?

To count multisets (not ordered sequences), fix an outer loop over each coin denomination and, inside it, an inner loop over amounts: this commits to considering each denomination once, so each multiset is counted exactly once.
Initialize dp[0] = 1 and dp[a] = 0 for a > 0. For each coin, for a from coin up to amount, do dp[a] += dp[a - coin]. Swapping these two loops would count ordered sequences instead. Return dp[amount].
